title: Independence
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 4). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: Name one reason why the Americans declared independence from Britain.
facts: In the 1760s, Britain had spent a lot of money on wars and wanted the colonists to help pay.
Britain added new taxes, like the Stamp Act on paper and a tax on tea. The colonists had no one to speak for them in Britain's government. They said: “No taxation without representation.”
In 1773, colonists in Boston threw British tea into the harbor to protest. This was the Boston Tea Party.
British soldiers stayed in Americans' houses, and the colonists did not have self-government.
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

newWords.meaning: paying taxes with no vote on them
to show in public that you disagree
a 1773 protest where colonists threw British tea into Boston Harbor

story.say: In the 1760s, Britain had spent a lot of money on wars. It wanted the colonists to help pay.

help.simpler: Britain needed money, so it asked the colonies to pay more.
help.example: Wars cost money for soldiers, ships and supplies.
help.why: This is where the road to independence starts.

story.say: Britain added new taxes, like the Stamp Act on paper and a tax on tea.

help.simpler: Colonists had to pay extra money on paper and on tea.
help.example: The Stamp Act taxed newspapers and other printed paper.
help.why: “High taxes” and “Stamp Act” are answers on the test.

story.say: The colonists had no one to speak for them in Britain’s government.

help.simpler: Britain made the taxes, but the colonists had no vote there.
help.example: No one from the colonies sat in Britain’s Parliament.
help.why: This is why the colonists said the taxes were unfair.

check.statement: The colonists had people to speak for them in Britain’s government.

story.say: They said: “No taxation without representation.”

help.simpler: They meant: no taxes unless we have a voice in the government.
help.example: Representation means someone speaks and votes for you.
help.why: “Taxation without representation” is an answer on the test.

story.say: In 1773, colonists in Boston threw British tea into the harbor to protest. This was the Boston Tea Party.

help.simpler: Colonists threw tea into the sea to show they were angry about the tax.
help.example: A protest is a way to show you do not agree.
help.why: “Boston Tea Party” is an answer on the test.

story.say: British soldiers stayed in Americans’ houses.

help.simpler: Families had to let British soldiers live in their homes.
help.example: Imagine soldiers you did not invite sleeping in your house.
help.why: This is another answer on the test.

check.prompt: Tap the protest in Boston in 1773.

story.say: And the colonists did not have self-government.

help.simpler: The colonists could not govern themselves. Britain decided for them.
help.example: Self-government: people choose their own leaders and laws.
help.why: “They did not have self-government” is an answer on the test.

story.say: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776.

help.simpler: On July 4, 1776, the colonies said they were free from Britain.
help.example: Adopted means it was officially accepted.
help.why: The test asks when the Declaration was adopted: July 4, 1776.

check.prompt: When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?

writeIt.sentence: We have Independence Day in July.

listen.explanationKey: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
facts: Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence.
He was the third President of the United States.
As President, he doubled the size of the United States with the Louisiana Purchase.

newWords.meaning: one of the people who started the country

story.say: Thomas Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence.

help.simpler: Jefferson is the writer of the Declaration.
help.example: Other leaders read his words and helped make changes.
help.why: The test asks who wrote the Declaration of Independence.

story.say: This is the Declaration of Independence. Jefferson wrote it.

help.simpler: These are the words Jefferson wrote.
help.example: It was adopted on July 4, 1776.
help.why: “Writer of the Declaration of Independence” is one thing he is famous for.

check.prompt: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?

story.say: He was the third President of the United States.

help.simpler: Two Presidents came before Jefferson. He was number three.
help.example: George Washington was the first President.
help.why: “Third President” is another answer on the test.

story.say: As President, he made the Louisiana Purchase: a huge area of land in the West.

help.simpler: The United States bought a very large piece of land.
help.example: It went from the Mississippi River to the Rocky Mountains.
help.why: This is one of the most famous things Jefferson did.

story.say: The Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the United States.

help.simpler: After the purchase, the country was two times as big.
help.example: Doubled means it became two times bigger.
help.why: “Doubled the size of the United States” is an answer on the test.

check.statement: Thomas Jefferson was the first President.

story.say: Jefferson is famous for the Declaration, for being President, and for the Louisiana Purchase.

help.simpler: Remember three things: writer, third President, Louisiana Purchase.
help.example: Any one of these is enough on the test.
help.why: The test asks you to name one thing Jefferson is famous for.

check.prompt: Thomas Jefferson is famous for many things. Name one.
choices: Doubled the size of the United States

listen.explanationKey: What war did the Americans fight to win independence from Britain?
facts: The Americans fought the American Revolution, also called the Revolutionary War, to win independence from Britain.
They fought because Britain would not let them govern themselves.
George Washington led the Continental Army.
Important events include the Battle of Bunker Hill, Washington crossing the Delaware, Valley Forge and the British surrender at Yorktown.

newWords.meaning: a fight to change who governs a country
to stop fighting and accept that you lost
the war from 1775 to 1783 that won independence from Britain for America

story.say: To win independence from Britain, the Americans fought a war: the American Revolution.

help.simpler: Americans fought Britain to become a free country.
help.example: Independence means being free to rule yourselves.
help.why: The test asks what war the Americans fought to win independence.

story.say: It is also called the Revolutionary War.

help.simpler: Two names, one war: the American Revolution, the Revolutionary War.
help.example: A revolution is a big change in who rules a country.
help.why: Both names are right answers on the test.

story.say: They fought because Britain would not let them govern themselves.

help.simpler: The colonists wanted to make their own decisions.
help.example: They wanted to choose their own leaders and laws.
help.why: This connects the war to the reasons for independence.

check.prompt: What war did the Americans fight to win independence from Britain?

story.say: George Washington led the Continental Army.

help.simpler: Washington was the general of the American army.
help.example: The Continental Army was the army of the colonies.
help.why: “General of the Continental Army” is an answer about Washington.

story.say: One important event was the Battle of Bunker Hill.

help.simpler: Bunker Hill was an early battle, near Boston.
help.example: A battle is one fight in a war.
help.why: “Bunker Hill” is an answer on the test.

story.say: Another was when Washington crossed the Delaware River with his army.

help.simpler: Washington took his army across a river in winter.
help.example: They crossed at night and won a battle at Trenton.
help.why: “Washington crossing the Delaware” is an answer on the test.

check.statement: George Washington led the Continental Army.

story.say: Another was Valley Forge, where the army camped through a hard winter.

help.simpler: The army stayed at Valley Forge in the cold and kept going.
help.example: An encampment is a camp where an army lives for a while.
help.why: “Valley Forge” is an answer on the test.

story.say: And at Yorktown, the British army surrendered.

help.simpler: At Yorktown, the British army gave up.
help.example: Surrender means to stop fighting and accept you lost.
help.why: “British surrender at Yorktown” is an answer on the test.

check.prompt: Tap the event where the British surrendered.
